{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Ernest Coleman''' (August 31, 1941 - January 17, 1990) was an American physicist working in the study, testing, and theory of [[Subatomic particle|sub-atomic particles]]. He was a professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Minnesota]] who held a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in physics from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Scott |date=January 3, 1999 |title=Ernest Coleman - Physicist of the African Diaspora |url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/physics/coleman_ernest.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918223914/https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/physics/coleman_ernest.html |archive-date=September 18, 2024 |access-date=November 20, 2024 |website=Buffalo Math}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Coleman was born on August 31, 1941, in Detroit, Michigan to parents James and Grace Coleman.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen0001unse_r3j9/page/1108/mode/2up |title=American men and women of science. The physical and biological sciences |date=1971 |publisher=New York : Bowker |url-access=registration |isbn=978-0-8352-0500-9 |pages=1108}}</ref> His parents were originally from Alabama.<ref name=":1" /> He gained his [[Bachelor of Science]] and [[Master of Science]] from the University of Michigan in 1963 and his Ph.D. in physics from the University of Michigan in 1966.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Black Contributors to Science and Energy Technology |url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED170154.pdf |access-date=2024-11-24 |publisher=Department of Energy, Washington D.C. Office of Public Affairs |page=28}}</ref> Coleman was a member of [[Phi Beta Kappa]].<ref name=":2" /> Coleman completed a one-year postdoctoral fellowship at the [[DESY]] research facility in [[Hamburg|Hamburg, Germany]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
After completing his [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellowship]], Coleman went on to obtain a position as an associate professor of physics at the University of Minnesota.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Martinez |first=J. V. |date=April 1, 1991 |title=Ernest Coleman |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/44/4/132/406539/Ernest-Coleman |journal=Physics Today |volume=44 |issue=4 |pages=132 |doi=10.1063/1.2810098 |bibcode=1991PhT....44d.132M |via=PUBS}}</ref> In 1974 he was employed as a researcher by the [[Federal government of the United States|United States Federal Government]]. That same year, Coleman was promoted to head of the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission|Atomic Energy Commission]]'s central laboratory research section within their division of physical research. His contributions to physics were related to the understanding of [[nucleon]] interactions at high energies.

Coleman was active in education, working as director of the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]] Summer Science Program from 1971 to 1984.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/840258275/?match=1&terms=%22ernest%20coleman%22%20physicist |title=SLAC summer program trains future scientists |work=[[Peninsula Times Tribune]] |date=September 11, 1971 |page=3 |via=newspapers.com }}</ref> He was president of the [[National Society of Black Physicists]] (NSBP) from 1984-1986.<ref name=":1"/> He also received the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1973<ref>{{cite report |url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/1970-1973_annual_reports.pdf |title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Annual Reports |chapter=Science and Technology |publisher=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |page=45 }}</ref> and the Distinguished Service Award of the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]] in 1977.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://portal.aapt.org//portal/AAPT_Awards.aspx |title=AAPT awards search |website=portal.aapt.org |publisher=[[American Association of Physics Teachers]] |access-date=January 14, 2025 }}, search '''Last Name'''=Coleman</ref> In 1976, he was honored as an [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society (1972–1997)#1976|American Physical Society (APS) Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?award_fellowship%5Bquery%5D=Ernest%20Coleman |title=APS Fellowship recipients |website=www.aps.org |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |access-date=January 14, 2025 }}</ref>

== Research ==
Coleman worked on experiments conducted at the [[Cosmotron]] at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and the [[Zero Gradient Synchrotron]] at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. There, he studied how [[proton]]s and [[meson]]s scattered from [[deuterium]] and [[hydrogen]] targets. As a result of Coleman's experiments testing the one-nucleon exchange model, a correction to [[Roy J. Glauber]]'s [[Scattering|scattering theory]] was discovered.<ref name=":0" />
